judgements.anchor: // Flags returns the complete FlagSet that applies
judgements.reason: Names and defines the accessor that returns the complete FlagSet applying to a command (local plus persistent declared here and by all parents); this is the mechanism a caller invokes to obtain the command's flags.
Defines the narrower accessor for flags declared on this command only, explaining which subset a caller gets; supports but does not alone satisfy the mode.

judgements.anchor: // InheritedFlags returns all flags which were inherited from parent commands.
judgements.reason: Defines the complementary accessor for the inherited subset, completing the set of list-of-flags accessors.

note: A1-A4 hold. Cobra defines the caller-facing accessors Flags(), LocalFlags(), LocalNonPersistentFlags(), InheritedFlags(), NonInheritedFlags() and PersistentFlags() on *Command; Flags() is documented at the pin as the complete set applying to the command. Answer writable from the pin alone.

judgements.anchor: // Flag climbs up the command tree looking for matching flag.
judgements.reason: Contains the mechanism: Command.Flag(name) looks the name up in this command's own FlagSet and, failing that, walks up the parent chain, returning the parent's flag (whose Value/DefValue the caller then reads).
States the essential condition: a parent's persistent flags are merged into the child's own FlagSet, so c.Flags().Get*(name) on the child resolves a parent-declared persistent flag's value.
Shows the parent lookup used by Flag(), including the parentsPflags set; explains the traversal but is unexported.

judgements.anchor: // Parent returns a commands parent command.
judgements.reason: The accessor that lets a caller reach the parent command explicitly and query its own flag set.

note: A1-A4 hold. The pin defines both routes: cmd.Flag(name) climbs the command tree, and mergePersistentFlags merges parent persistent flags into the child's FlagSet so cmd.Flags() resolves them; Parent() gives direct access. No runtime state or external material needed.

judgements.reason: The source-defined switch that makes Cobra stop interpreting hyphen-prefixed tokens as flags: when set, all flags are passed through to the command as arguments.
The condition that implements it: ParseFlags returns immediately without parsing when DisableFlagParsing is set.
Shows the consequence during execution: with parsing disabled the raw argument slice, hyphens included, is handed to the command instead of the parsed residue.
The other pinned lever: a bare -- terminates flag scanning, so following hyphenated tokens are treated as plain arguments.

note: Direct conditional yes with a source-defined mechanism: set Command.DisableFlagParsing (or terminate with --). A1-A4 hold; the semantics are documented inside the pinned Go files, not only in pflag.

judgements.anchor: // SetArgs sets arguments for the command.
judgements.reason: The caller operation for supplying the target subcommand name and its flags programmatically instead of os.Args[1:].

judgements.anchor: // Execute uses the args (os.Args[1:] by default)
judgements.reason: States the dispatch mechanism: Execute runs the supplied args through the command tree, matching the command and then its corresponding flags.
Essential condition for the procedure: execution is always redirected to the root, so the args must be set on (or resolvable from) the root command.

note: A1-A4 hold. The pinned procedure for invoking one command from another with flags is root.SetArgs([]string{sub, --flag, value}) followed by Execute/ExecuteC, which re-dispatches from the root and parses the flags of the matched command.

D4: the honest answer at the pin is only that multi-character short flags are not supported. Positive evidence inside the pinned tree: command.go:631-641 (shortHasNoOptDefVal) resolves a short token with fs.ShorthandLookup(name[:1]), i.e. exactly one character; command.go:664 recognises the single-dash form only when len(s) == 2; command.go:1467-1480 renders a shorthand as -+f.Shorthand. No API, field, option or documented procedure anywhere in the pinned tree registers or accepts a shorthand longer than one character, and the registration/validation of shorthands lives in github.com/spf13/pflag v1.0.5 (go.mod), which is not part of the pinned tree. Converting that absence into a grade-3 span is what D4 forbids.

judgements.anchor: // legacyArgs validation has the following behaviour:
judgements.reason: The default mechanism and its conditions: a root command that has subcommands rejects an unrecognised first argument with an unknown command error plus suggestions; subcommands accept arbitrary args unless Args is set.

judgements.anchor: // NoArgs returns an error if any args are included.
judgements.reason: The caller-facing procedure to get the same rejection on any command: set Args: cobra.NoArgs, which returns the unknown command error for the first stray argument.
Shows how the Did you mean this? suggestion text is appended to the unknown-subcommand error and which command fields gate it.
The tuning knobs a caller sets to control or disable the suggestion behaviour that accompanies a wrong subcommand.

note: A1-A4 hold. The pin defines both the built-in handling (legacyArgs producing unknown command %q for %q plus suggestions, surfaced by ExecuteC) and the caller levers (Args: NoArgs/OnlyValidArgs, SuggestFor, DisableSuggestions, SuggestionsMinimumDistance, SilenceErrors).

D3: BoolVar is not defined anywhere in the pinned tree. It is a method of pflag.FlagSet from github.com/spf13/pflag v1.0.5, declared as a requirement in go.mod at the pin but not part of the pinned repository, so its signature and the type of its default-value parameter, the facts the question turns on, exist only outside the pin. Positive evidence at the pin: every Cobra call site passes a concrete bool default rather than any nil-like value (completions.go:745, 784, 809, 835 use Flags().BoolVar(&noDesc, ..., compCmdNoDescFlagDefault, ...); command.go:1218 and 1220 use BoolP/Bool with false). Nothing in the pinned tree defines, documents or permits a nil default for a boolean flag. (The same finding also reads as D4, since the honest answer is that this is not supported; D3 is recorded because the API named in the question is wholly outside the pinned tree.)

judgements.reason: The source-defined mechanism for replacing the whole usage rendering, which is where flag defaults are emitted, with the application's own function.
The lighter form of the same mechanism: substitute a usage template whose flag section does not render defaults.
Identifies exactly where the default template delegates the whole Flags/Global Flags block, and therefore what must be replaced to suppress defaults.
Corroborates that a caller can iterate the flag set itself and choose which of Name, Shorthand, DefValue and Value to print.

note: Conditional yes. Cobra exposes no dedicated switch for suppressing default values, but the pin does define an affirmative caller procedure: the entire flag block of the help output comes from the default usage template (command.go:544-582), and SetUsageTemplate / SetUsageFunc / SetHelpFunc replace it. The answer is therefore more than the capability is unsupported, so D4 does not apply; A1-A4 hold on the pinned Go bytes.

judgements.anchor: // AddCommand adds one or more commands to this parent command.
judgements.reason: The caller operation that makes a command a child of the parent, which is what puts it in the parent's command list rendered under Available Commands.

judgements.anchor: // IsAvailableCommand determines if a command is available as a non-help command
judgements.reason: The exact conditions an added command must satisfy to appear in that section: not Deprecated, not Hidden, not the parent's help command, and either Runnable or having available subcommands.
The template line that emits the section, showing it iterates .Commands filtered by IsAvailableCommand.

note: A1-A4 hold. Procedure at the pin: construct a *Command with Use/Short and a Run (or subcommands), attach it with parent.AddCommand, and keep Hidden/Deprecated unset so IsAvailableCommand returns true; the default usage template then lists it under Available Commands.

judgements.reason: Establishes the mechanism and its meaning at the pin: Cobra itself decides whether a flag was actually supplied by the user by testing the flag's Changed field, treating !Changed as not set.
Second independent use of the same mechanism, recording per flag whether it is set from Changed.
Shows the complementary accessors a caller reads: DefValue holds the declared default while Value holds the current value.

note: A1-A4 hold. Procedure at the pin: look the flag up (cmd.Flags().Lookup(name) or cmd.Flag(name)) and read Changed, which Cobra itself uses to mean the user supplied it; DefValue is the declared default and Value the current value. Source-defined rule, not runtime state, so D2 does not apply.

judgements.anchor: PersistentPreRun: children of this command will inherit and execute.
judgements.reason: The caller-facing hook and its essential properties: the ordered *Run chain, the fact that all hooks receive the executed command and the arguments after the command name, and that PersistentPreRun is inherited by children.

The mechanism itself: on every execution Cobra walks from the executed command up its parents and invokes the persistent pre-run hook with the executed command and its argument slice, so a single root hook observes every invocation.

judgements.anchor: // CommandPath returns the full path to this command.
judgements.reason: The accessor that yields the identity to record for the executed command.

judgements.anchor: // CalledAs returns the command name or alias that was used to invoke
judgements.reason: The accessor for the exact name or alias the user typed, complementing CommandPath when recording an invocation.

note: Read as how does one record executed commands and parameters. A1-A4 hold: the pinned procedure is to set PersistentPreRun/PersistentPreRunE on the root command, which Cobra invokes for every executed command with that command and its non-flag args, and to read CommandPath()/CalledAs() plus cmd.Flags() inside it. This is a source-defined rule, not an observation of a particular run, so D2 does not apply.

judgements.anchor: // MarkFlagsRequiredTogether marks the given flags with annotations so that Cobra errors
judgements.reason: The caller procedure and its condition: call c.MarkFlagsRequiredTogether(names...) after the flags are declared, and Cobra errors when the command is invoked with a subset but not all of them, i.e. one flag requires the other.

judgements.anchor: are set they must all be set
judgements.reason: The enforcement that gives the marking its meaning, including the error text raised when part of the group is supplied.
Tracked documentation at the pin stating the dependency case explicitly and showing the two-step registration; supporting only, the Go span carries answerability.

note: A1-A4 hold. Cobra's mechanism for making one flag depend on another is the flag-group annotation API in flag_groups.go, principally MarkFlagsRequiredTogether (with MarkFlagsOneRequired and MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive as siblings), enforced from execute() via ValidateFlagGroups. A complete answer must note the dependency is symmetric (all-or-none), which the cited bytes state.

judgements.anchor: // InheritedFlags returns all flags which were inherited from parent commands.
judgements.reason: The mechanism under test and the accessor used to assert on it: it merges persistent flags first, then returns exactly the parent-declared flags not shadowed locally.

The essential precondition: the parents' persistent flags are only present after the merge that InheritedFlags/LocalFlags/ParseFlags perform, which is why a test must query through those accessors or after execution.

judgements.anchor: // HasInheritedFlags checks if the command has flags inherited from its parent command.
judgements.reason: The boolean predicate a test can assert directly.

judgements.anchor: // SetArgs sets arguments for the command.
judgements.reason: The pinned entry point for driving a command in a test, documented as particularly useful when testing, so an inherited flag can be exercised end to end.

note: A1-A4 hold under either reading of test (inspect, or drive from a Go test): build the parent/child tree, use root.SetArgs plus Execute to supply the flag, and assert via child.InheritedFlags()/HasInheritedFlags() or child.Flags().Get*(name), which resolve after mergePersistentFlags.

judgements.reason: Cobra's own registration of the single-dash form: the flag is declared with the P variant, whose second argument is the one-letter shorthand, which is exactly how -h becomes usable instead of --help.
The source-defined condition distinguishing the two forms during argument scanning: a double-dash token is the long name, while the single-dash form is recognised only as - plus one character.
Confirms the single-dash token is resolved through the shorthand table using its first character only.
Tracked documentation at the pin showing the same registration with the shorthand argument; supporting only.

note: A1-A4 hold. The pinned answer covers the whole query: the single-dash form is the shorthand form, obtained by registering the flag with a P-variant that takes a one-character shorthand (Cobra does this itself for -h/--help), and single-dash long names are not a separate feature because the scanner only accepts - plus one character.

judgements.anchor: // SetHelpTemplate sets help template to be used.
judgements.reason: The caller mechanism for controlling the order in which help output sections are emitted, hence for putting any section first.
The default layout being changed, and the resolution rule: a template set on the command wins, otherwise the parent's is inherited; the default puts Long/Short first and then the usage string.
The companion setter for the usage half of the output, whose default template fixes the order of Usage, Aliases, Examples, Available Commands, Flags and the help footer.

judgements.anchor: EnableCommandSorting controls sorting of the slice of commands
judgements.reason: If the intent is to move the help command to the head of the command list, this is the pinned switch: disable sorting and the commands appear in AddCommand order.

note: A1-A4 hold. Q is terse and does not say which help element is meant, but every reading resolves to the same pinned mechanism: the layout of help/usage output is entirely template-driven, and SetHelpTemplate/SetUsageTemplate (or SetHelpFunc/SetUsageFunc) let the application reorder it, with EnableCommandSorting=false covering the ordering of the help command in the command list. Flagging the wording ambiguity rather than rewriting the rubric.

judgements.reason: Contains the operation and its condition side by side: register with BoolP(name, shorthand, ...) to attach the shorthand, or with the plain variant when the shorthand letter is already taken, showing exactly which argument is the shorthand.
Cobra performing the procedure itself when it declares --help with the shorthand h on the command's flag set.
Tracked documentation at the pin showing the same P-suffixed registration on both PersistentFlags and Flags; supporting only.

note: A1-A4 hold. Procedure at the pin: declare the flag on cmd.Flags() or cmd.PersistentFlags() with the P-suffixed variant, passing the single-character shorthand as the argument after the long name; the shorthand must not already be registered on that flag set, which is the condition Cobra itself checks with ShorthandLookup before adding -v.

judgements.anchor: If this is true all flags will be passed to the command as arguments.
judgements.reason: The mechanism for a command whose flag set cannot be known in advance: set DisableFlagParsing so every token, flags included, reaches the command as an argument to forward to the script.
The condition that implements it during execution: with parsing disabled Run/RunE receives the raw, unstripped argument slice.

judgements.anchor: // ArgsLenAtDash will return the length of c.Flags().Args at the moment
judgements.reason: The alternative when only the tail is unknown: keep parsing the command's own flags, separate the pass-through arguments with --, and use ArgsLenAtDash to find the split point.
The positional-args validator to set so an arbitrary number of forwarded operands is accepted.

note: A1-A4 hold. Q asks how to build a command that runs a script file while its flags are not known in advance; the pinned answer is DisableFlagParsing (whole argv forwarded) or the -- terminator with ArgsLenAtDash, plus Args: ArbitraryArgs. All spans are pinned Go with the semantics stated in the tree.

judgements.anchor: If c already has help flag, it will do nothing.
judgements.reason: The condition that makes it possible: Cobra adds its combined BoolP(help, h, ...) flag only when no flag named help already exists, so an application that declares its own --help (without a shorthand) and a separate -h flag keeps the two spellings as distinct flags.

The mechanism that decides the outcome: execute() short-circuits to the help path purely on the boolean value of the flag named help, which is why the default single flag makes -h and --help indistinguishable and why splitting them into two flags separates the behaviour.
Shows in Cobra's own code that a shorthand letter can already belong to a different flag than the long name being registered, so the long form and the single-letter form need not be the same flag.
The hook for customising what the help path does once it is reached.

note: Conditional yes, not D4. With Cobra's defaults the two are the same flag (one BoolP registration, one GetBool(help) check), so they cannot differ; but the pinned source positively provides the way to separate them, because InitDefaultHelpFlag stands down whenever a flag named help already exists, letting the application register --help and -h as two distinct flags and handle them separately. A1-A4 hold on that affirmative route.
